text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty P1 - GPU pool 'swarm-hive' saturation + driver/runtime errors (Xid/OOM). Page sent to oncall @Alex and @Ryan.

PagerDuty: Triggered at 2026-03-15T01:12:02Z — high queue growth observed for model-serving route /v1/generate (swarm-hive).

Alex: I'm on it — seeing a sustained request backlog ~12k, tail latency 95th > 6s for several routes. Dashboards show queue length climbing since ~00:45 UTC.

Ryan: Joining. Autoscaler logs show repeated failures: `scale_up failed: max_nodes_reached (600/600)`. We appear to have hit our hard node cap for the region.

InfraBot: Autoscaler event: desired_nodes=620, provisioned=600, cap=600, reason='quota_limit'. Recent scale attempts at 00:50, 00:52, 01:05 UTC.

Sara: Also seeing repeated CUDA Xid 63 / GPU OOM traces across 5 different nodes in pool. Suspect driver/runtime instability reducing effective capacity (nodes are technically up but GPUs are unusable). Sample from /var/log/kern.log:

```
[01:07:11] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:3b:00): 63, pid=8743, GPU=0, Channel ID=1
[01:07:11] kernel: nvidia: GPU watchdog timeout - resetting channel
[01:07:12] kernel: Out of memory: Killed process 15234 (python) total-vm:5120000kB, anon-rss:4200000kB
```

Maya: Customers impacted: acme-inc and nova-ai seeing timeouts and error spikes. Early estimate: ~10-15% of hosted inference traffic experiencing degradation.

Alex: Immediate mitigation plan I'm executing now: 1) Pause new policy-based admissions to swarm-hive routes to stop inflow (short-term). 2) Reroute high-priority customer traffic to warm-standby pool 'swarm-warm' (lower capacity but stable). 3) Try rolling driver restart on most-affected nodes.

Alex: Pausing admissions with admin toggle: `POST /admin/route/swarm-hive/admits/pause` -> 200 OK. Rerouting config applied for acme/nova.

Ryan: I attempted a driver restart on gpu-42 (one of the hot nodes):

```
ssh gpu-42
sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver.service
# restart returned exit 1
journalctl -u nvidia-driver -n 80 --no-pager shows crash loop with OOMs
```

Ryan: dmesg on gpu-42 shows kernel OOM killing nvidia modules during restart attempt:

```
[01:09:02] kernel: nvidia-modeset: loading out-of-tree module taints kernel.
[01:09:02] kernel: nvidia-modeset: probe failed with error -12
[01:09:03] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4082 (nvidia-modeset) score 1000 or sacrifice child
```

InfraBot: Hotpatch candidate detected: driver rollback to 535.54.03 has good health signal on canary nodes (2/2).

OpsLead: Good — coordinate a small canary roll to 6 nodes, monitor Xid and OOM metrics. If stable for 10m, escalate to batch roll. Meanwhile, we need to free up capacity: mark 8 most-flappy nodes as drain candidates and move running pods to 'swarm-warm' and dedicated reserved pool. Use `kubectl drain` carefully.

Alex: Draining gpu-42 now: `kubectl drain gpu-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — pod eviction started. Moving long-running jobs to reserved pool requires manual patch to scheduling labels.

Ryan: We're also hitting autoscaler limit in cloud account. Filed manual quota bump with cloud infra (ticket CLD-98721) and requested temporary manual override to 660 nodes to allow autoscale until midnight UTC. Cloud team acknowledged with ETA ~15m.

Sara: Adding temporary admission control rule to fail-fast low-priority requests so we don't overwhelm queues while autoscale is catching up.

CustomerEng: Drafting status page update: "We are experiencing partial degradation of hosted inference due to GPU driver instability and capacity constraints. We have mitigations in place (traffic rerouted, driver rollback in progress). Some customers may see increased latencies or errors. Next update in 30 minutes." Approving now.

Alex: Rolling driver rollback to 6 canary nodes (confirmed infra test). Command used on canaries:

```
ssh canary-node-1
sudo apt-get install nvidia-driver-535=535.54.03 -y
sudo reboot
```

InfraBot: Canary nodes show GPU metrics back to normal within 2m after reboot. Xid and OOM error rates dropped to baseline.

Ryan: After canary success, started batch roll on 24 low-risk nodes. Watchers assigned: @Sara (metrics), @Alex (evictions), @Maya (customer comms).

OpsLead: Keep an eye on scheduling pressure. If node capacity still below need after driver roll and quota bump, we'll implement longer-term mitigations: prewarmed nodes, reservation for high-priority customers, and circuit-breaker for model routes.

Alex: Autoscaler manual override applied to 660 by Cloud team at 01:34 UTC. We scaled up ~40 nodes; backlog reduced to ~3k in 6 minutes. Tail latencies improving.

Maya: Noted — acme reports errors dropped to near zero after reroute. Nova still sees intermittent priority queue timeouts (they are hit hardest by long sequences). Working with them on per-tenant throttles.

Ryan: Observed one node (gpu-57) remain flappy after driver rollback — kernel OOM persists and process restarts fail. Marked for replacement. Creating maintenance request to reprovision gpu-57.

Alex: Created incident ticket INC-2026-3642, summary and actions logged.

IncidentBot: Incident INC-2026-3642 created, severity: P1, status: mitigating. Runbook invoked: gpu-capacity-degen.

OpsLead: Handoff checklist for night oncall (assigned to @Maya at 02:00 UTC):
- Ensure driver roll completes across all nodes.
- Confirm autoscaler remains at override until quota/backfill stable.
- Watch queue length and tail latencies for re-regressions.
- Confirm replacements for nodes flagged for reprovision (gpu-57).
- Update status page on resolution and timeline.

Maya: Ack — I'll take the night handoff. Current state summary for handoff message: backlog down from 12k -> 2.8k; tail latency 95th from 6s -> 2.1s; autoscaler override active (660 cap) until 06:00 UTC; driver rollback in progress (canary success, batch ~24/120 nodes done); 3 nodes flagged for reprovision.

CustomerEng: Posting 01:46 UTC update to status page and notifying enterprise contacts (acme, nova).

Alex: Leaving notes in the incident ticket for follow-ups: consider increasing warm-standby pool size, add postmortem item for autoscaler cap + contingency docs, and add safety to driver rollout pipeline to catch memory leaks earlier.

Ryan: One more: add metric alert for Xid spikes per pool (threshold low) — will open follow-up ticket.

Maya: Good handoff. I'll broadcast any major regressions and escalate to eng-sre if we see new OOM waves. :thumbsup:

Alex: Thanks everyone. Leaving channel but reachable by DM.

IncidentBot: Update: last_message_ts set to 3642002225. Incident remains in mitigating state."
